origin.description: S3 generic that downloads or copies the source bundle for a remote.

arguments.name: quiet
arguments.text: If TRUE, suppress output. Default FALSE.

origin.details: A local remote copies the directory into a new temporary directory. file.copy nests the source directory under that temporary directory, and the return value is the first entry there. A GitHub remote downloads repos/{user}/{repo}/tarball/{ref} to a temporary .tar.gz file. quiet suppresses the GitHub download message.
origin.value: Path to the copied directory or the downloaded archive.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile()
dir.create(path)
writeLines(c("Package: foo", "Version: 1.0.0"), file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION"))
bundle <- remotes:::remote_download(remotes:::local_remote(path))
name <- read.dcf(file.path(bundle, "DESCRIPTION"))[1, "Package"]
cat(paste0("remote_download on a local directory copies a directory whose DESCRIPTION says Package: ", name, ".\n"))

translation.description: S3 generic that downloads or copies the source bundle for a remote.

arguments.name: quiet
arguments.text: If True, suppress the GitHub download message. Default False. The local method accepts it and does not print.

translation.details: A local remote copies the directory into a new temporary directory and returns that copy. Compare the Package field of its DESCRIPTION with the source, not the temporary path. A GitHub remote saves the tarball from repos/{user}/{repo}/tarball/{ref}. ref is URL-encoded with reserved characters encoded. The request uses urllib. The token is the remote's auth_token.
translation.value: Path to the copied directory or the downloaded .tar.gz file.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile
from remotes.remote import local_remote, remote_download
path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
with open(os.path.join(path, "DESCRIPTION"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
    handle.write("Package: foo\nVersion: 1.0.0\n")
bundle = remote_download(local_remote(path))
with open(os.path.join(bundle, "DESCRIPTION"), encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    name = next(line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in handle if line.startswith("Package:"))
print("remote_download on a local directory copies a directory whose DESCRIPTION says Package: " + name + ".")
